findings.body: Raise: Not done. The changed stub writes README.md as LF bytes, but its upgraded-client path still writes forge.toml with write_text at line 97. On Windows, that produces CRLF; the test Git configuration in tests/conftest.py:305-314 disables system configuration and sets no core.autocrlf conversion. The resulting commit retains CRLF, while test_2 compares it with the LF-only upgraded string at line 247. That Windows case still fails.
findings.title: Not done: Main's full test run passes on Windows and macOS as on Linux: test stubs read stdin as UTF-8 and write files with Unix line ending

findings.body: Raise: Test. The changed test replaces each Windows timeout expression with its non-Windows fallback before asserting 120/150 seconds. tests/test_ci_job_budgets.py:52-53 checks only that the effective timeout is below the job cap. Reverting the Windows 270/300-second limits to 120/150 would therefore leave these tests green, although the longer Windows budget is a named Done-when behavior.
findings.title: Not done: Windows per-test timeout budget test

findings.body: Raise: Gate. The proof list says the npm-cache and macOS Go setup are proven by main's full CI run, but the changed steps belong to a job that is explicitly skipped on pull requests (.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:42). This branch has no pull-request check behind that claimed full-run proof, so the Windows and macOS outcome cannot be verified before merge.
